name: Adele Gomez
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember an alarm bell that used to wake a whole street.” On Wednesday, near the bank steps, Adele takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I collect clocks that measure something worth waiting for. This is the first the owner refused to sell.
appearance: Adele has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Look for a gray streak running back from the forehead. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a narrow-striped sweater with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. In conversation Adele draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
personality: Adele treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To document the clock in place with permission.
family: Silas Murphy is Adele’s half-sibling. Adele saves a place. Silas chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *A shelf of apologies*, Silas says, “I used to write apologies for my boss. This is the first one I signed with my own name.”
connections: Shay Stein. The returning collector gets the true account of why a dealer sold the clock.
